title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
venue: NAACL-HLT 2019, Volume 1, pp. 4171-4186
note: Bidirectional pretraining supports task adaptation through fine-tuning with an additional output layer.

title: Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning at Scale
note: Introduces XLM-R and studies multilingual pretraining scale, transfer and capacity trade-offs.

title: MuRIL: Multilingual Representations for Indian Languages
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2103.10730
note: MuRIL emphasizes Indian-language representations and incorporates translated and transliterated document pairs.

title: LinCE: A Centralized Benchmark for Linguistic Code-switching Evaluation
venue: Twelfth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC 2020), pp. 1803-1813
note: Consolidates code-switching corpora and multiple tasks, including sentiment analysis, for comparable evaluation.

title: Corpus Creation and Emotion Prediction for Hindi-English Code-Mixed Social Media Text
venue: NAACL-HLT 2018: Student Research Workshop, pp. 128-135
note: Provides Hindi-English tweets annotated for emotion, token language and the language expressing the emotion.

title: Attention Is All You Need
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
note: Introduces the Transformer architecture using attention in place of recurrence for sequence transduction.

title: How Multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
note: Probes multilingual BERT transfer, including code-switching, and identifies systematic language-pair limitations.

title: XTREME: A Massively Multilingual Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-lingual Generalisation
venue: ICML 2020, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 119, pp. 4411-4421
note: Evaluates cross-lingual transfer across 40 languages and nine tasks, revealing substantial variation across languages.

title: GLUECoS: An Evaluation Benchmark for Code-Switched NLP
note: Benchmarks six code-switching tasks and investigates additional adaptation on generated code-switched text.

title: SemEval-2020 Task 9: Overview of Sentiment Analysis of Code-Mixed Tweets
venue: Fourteenth Workshop on Semantic Evaluation, pp. 774-790
note: SentiMix provides Hindi-English and Spanish-English tweets with three sentiment-polarity labels.

title: GoEmotions: A Dataset of Fine-Grained Emotions
note: Provides human annotations for English Reddit comments using 27 emotion categories and neutral.

title: SemEval-2018 Task 1: Affect in Tweets
venue: 12th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation, pp. 1-17
note: Separates emotion classification and intensity from valence subtasks across English, Arabic and Spanish.

title: Using millions of emoji occurrences to learn any-domain representations for detecting sentiment, emotion and sarcasm
note: Uses emoji prediction as distant supervision to learn transferable affective representations.

title: Sentiment of Emojis
venue: PLOS ONE 10(12), article e0144296
note: Constructs an emoji sentiment lexicon from sentiment-annotated tweets across 13 European languages.

title: SemEval 2018 Task 2: Multilingual Emoji Prediction
venue: 12th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation, pp. 24-33
note: Benchmarks emoji prediction from English and Spanish tweet text using macro F-score.

title: SemEval-2018 Task 3: Irony Detection in English Tweets
venue: 12th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation, pp. 39-50
note: Defines binary and fine-grained irony tasks with manually annotated tweets and removed collection hashtags.

title: “Did you really mean what you said?” : Sarcasm Detection in Hindi-English Code-Mixed Data using Bilingual Word Embeddings
venue: Sixth Workshop on Noisy User-generated Text (W-NUT 2020), pp. 7-15
note: Provides a labelled Hinglish sarcasm dataset and evaluates neural approaches using bilingual embeddings.

title: Sarcasm Analysis Using Conversation Context
venue: Computational Linguistics 44(4), pp. 755-792
note: Compares contextual and current-turn sarcasm models on Twitter and discussion-forum data.

title: MELD: A Multimodal Multi-Party Dataset for Emotion Recognition in Conversations
note: Provides multi-party dialogue emotion annotations and evaluates contextual and multimodal baselines.

title: SemEval 2024 - Task 10: Emotion Discovery and Reasoning its Flip in Conversation (EDiReF)
venue: 18th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval-2024), pp. 1933-1946
note: Defines emotion recognition and emotion-flip reasoning using manually annotated English and Hindi-English conversations.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
venue: ICML 2017, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70, pp. 1321-1330
note: Studies neural-network miscalibration and temperature scaling as a post-processing calibration method.

title: Can you trust your model's uncertainty? Evaluating predictive uncertainty under dataset shift
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019)
note: Shows that calibration and uncertainty quality can deteriorate under dataset shift.

title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
note: Evaluates ensembles of neural predictors for predictive uncertainty and out-of-distribution behavior.

title: Divergence measures based on the Shannon entropy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 37(1), pp. 145-151
note: Introduces Shannon-entropy-based divergence measures, including the Jensen-Shannon construction.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
note: Studies selective prediction and the trade-off between accepted-instance coverage and classification risk.

title: Dealing with Disagreements: Looking Beyond the Majority Vote in Subjective Annotations
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 10, pp. 92-110
note: Models individual annotators and shows that preserving disagreement can improve modeling of subjective judgments.

title: The “Problem” of Human Label Variation: On Ground Truth in Data, Modeling and Evaluation
note: Distinguishes meaningful human label variation from annotation mistakes and discusses implications for evaluation.

title: Datasheets for Datasets
venue: Communications of the ACM
note: Proposes systematic documentation of dataset motivation, composition, collection, uses and maintenance.

title: Data Statements for Natural Language Processing: Toward Mitigating System Bias and Enabling Better Science
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 6, pp. 587-604
note: Argues that dataset language and population documentation improves the precision of generalization claims.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
note: Introduces capability-oriented behavioral tests that reveal failures hidden by aggregate held-out accuracy.

title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
venue: ACL 2018, Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 1383-1392
note: Explains how task, evaluation measure and experimental design determine appropriate significance tests.
